title: When Trade Compresses: The Impact of Liberalization on Wage Inequality
affiliations: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, Bank of Portugal - Research Department and Independent

detail.title: When Trade Compresses: The Impact of Liberalization on Wage Inequality

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Cleveland Working Paper No. 26-01
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study the effects of trade liberalization on the full wage distribution, exploiting Spain's 1993 entry into the European Single Market. Using employer-employee data, we identify the causal effects of trade across the entire wage distribution, using a novel shift-share instrument embedded in an unconditional quantile regression. We find that the liberalization reduced wage inequality, leading to wage compression through earnings gains at the bottom of the distribution and wage losses at the top. We trace this compression to two asymmetric channels: import competition disproportionately harmed high earners, while export opportunities benefited low earners. The key mechanism is an import-driven “skill-downgrading.” A multi-region multi-sector model shows that the key insight for understanding these empirical results is that trade's distributional effects depend on the skill intensity of a country's tradable sector, and Spain's was relatively low-skill intensive back then.

title: Beyond Digital Wills: A Global Review of Posthumous Data Governance, AI Risks, and Digital Dignity with Implications for Pakistan
affiliations: Faisalabad College of Law

detail.title: Beyond Digital Wills: A Global Review of Posthumous Data Governance, AI Risks, and Digital Dignity with Implications for Pakistan
detail.abstract: This review looks into digital identities, individual data, and machine created profiles shaping existence beyond death. Combining worldwide findings on online afterlife control, privacy when deceased, along with dangers tied to smart systems-special attention goes to Pakistan's laws, customs, and Muslim perspectives. Current work suggests digital remnants involve social network footprints, files kept remotely, plus automatic results still active following someone's passing. Outside sources point out weak platform guidelines, confusing inheritance procedures, alongside growing software capable of mimicking speech or appearance, sparking fresh debates around respect, abuse, and permission. Still, Pakistan rarely appears in such conversations-even though societal and faith-based norms place a high value on reputation, confidentiality, and heritage once dead. This study fills the gap by examining strategies from the EU, USA, Malaysia, UAE, and India, followed by evaluating how they apply to Pakistan. Rather than just summarizing, it combines moral, regulatory, and societal perspectives to shape a locally relevant Digital Dignity Framework. Instead of copying global models, it links worldwide norms with Islamic values and community practices, suggesting ways toward fairer, more responsible management of digital afterlives.

title: Farmers' Perception and Satisfaction with Digital Farming Applications for Crop Management

detail.title: Farmers' Perception and Satisfaction with Digital Farming Applications for Crop Management
detail.abstract: This study investigates farmers' perception and satisfaction with digital farming applications designed for crop management, examining how usability, relevance of information, and overall user experience shape adoption outcomes. A mixed-method research design was employed, integrating structured surveys, observational app-use sessions, and semi-structured interviews to capture both measurable satisfaction indicators and in-depth user insights. Quantitative data assessed perceived usefulness, ease of use, content quality, and satisfaction levels, while qualitative findings explored contextual challenges such as digital literacy, network limitations, and trust in digital recommendations (Adebayo et al. 2023; Mensah and Adomako 2022; Wanjiru 2021). Results show that farmers generally value the timely advice, decision-support tools, and visual learning features offered by digital applications; however, satisfaction decreases when apps are difficult to navigate, contain technical language, or fail to reflect local farming realities (Okeke 2024; Ibrahim and Musa 2023). Limited linguistic customization, inconsistent internet connectivity, and low smartphone proficiency also emerged as major barriers. The study concludes that while digital farming applications have strong potential to enhance crop management, sustainable adoption depends on culturally relevant content, intuitive interface design, and ongoing farmer support systems.

title: Anthroporesource Dynamics (ARD): A Framework for Individual Resource and Institutional Context

detail.title: Anthroporesource Dynamics (ARD): A Framework for Individual Resource and Institutional Context

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants and therefore did not require ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently.

detail.abstract: Anthroporesource Dynamics (ARD) is proposed as an integrative conceptual framework for analyzing an individual’s resource configuration within institutional contexts. ARD identifies six fundamental categories of personal resources—energy, skills, social capital, financial capital, power, and time—and introduces the concept of an Institutional Modifier (IM), defined as “the set of rules, norms, infrastructures, cultural codes, and enforcement mechanisms that determine the value, convertibility, and accessibility of resources in a given institutional environment.” Within ARD, three key dynamic mechanisms are considered: conversion (the transformation of one resource into another), aggregation (the combination of resources), and acceleration (the self-reinforcing growth or decline of resources) . The theoretical foundations of ARD draw on classic sociological and political-economic insights: the diversity of capital forms and their convertibility (Bourdieu 1986; 1990; 1998), the nature of social legitimacy and authority (Weber 1978) and power in social exchange (Blau 1964), social facts and institutional norms as external constraints (Durkheim 1982; North 1990), material conditions and means of production (Marx and Engels 1970), the concept of social capital and network structure (Coleman 1988; Granovetter 1973; Burt 1992), and the conservation of resources in psychology (Hobfoll 1989; 2001), among others . ARD is presented as an initial conceptual model intended to link the individual’s micro-level resources with the institutional context while avoiding reductionism and determinism . This work is theoretical in nature, does not claim exhaustive explanatory power, and emphasizes the need for further mathematical formalization and empirical research to support and refine the framework .

title: Toward a Unified Model of AI-Native Networking: Integrating Autonomous Healing, Zero Trust, and Real-Time Data Exchange

detail.title: Toward a Unified Model of AI-Native Networking: Integrating Autonomous Healing, Zero Trust, and Real-Time Data Exchange
detail.abstract: AI-native networking has emerged as a critical engineering paradigm capable of supporting the growing demands of distributed, latency-sensitive, and security-critical systems, yet current research treats autonomous healing, zero-trust security, and real-time data exchange as separate domains (Balakrishnan, 2022; Balakrishnan, 2023; Balakrishnan, 2024). This study develops a unified conceptual model that integrates cognitive autonomous networking, federated zero-trust enforcement, and synchronized real-time state exchange into a single architectural framework, using a qualitative synthesis of leading scholarly works. Findings demonstrate that the convergence of real-time data streams with cognitive healing and adaptive trust policies establishes a more resilient, self-governing network capable of mitigating adversarial risks, reducing latency, and enabling multi-cloud synchronization (Demertzis et al., 2019; Asheralieva and Niyato, 2022). The proposed architecture offers theoretical clarity and practical pathways for next-generation AI-native infrastructures while acknowledging methodological and contextual limitations inherent in conceptual modeling. This work concludes by outlining future research priorities for simulation, validation, and global-scale deployment.

title: Cognitive Trust, Autonomous Control, and Real-Time Data Processing in Modern Distributed Networks

detail.title: Cognitive Trust, Autonomous Control, and Real-Time Data Processing in Modern Distributed Networks
detail.abstract: The increasing complexity of modern distributed networks, particularly those spanning multi-cloud infrastructures, has introduced critical challenges in network reliability, security, and real-time performance. This study investigates the integration of cognitive trust mechanisms, autonomous network control, and real-time data processing as a unified framework for modern distributed networks. By synthesizing approaches such as the Real-Time State Information Exchange Protocol (RTSIX), Cognitive Autonomous Networking (CAN), AI-Native Zero-Trust Architecture (AI-ZTA), and adaptive AI-driven packet inspection, this research demonstrates the potential of federated AI systems to enhance operational resilience. Simulation results indicate that the proposed integrated framework significantly reduces failover recovery time, optimizes latency-sensitive operations, and enforces dynamic trust across multi-cloud environments. The study concludes that incorporating cognitive trust and autonomous control mechanisms within distributed networks is essential for maintaining secure, reliable, and efficient operations, particularly for latency-critical applications and globally distributed infrastructures (Balakrishnan, 2022; Balakrishnan, 2024; Demertzis et al., 2019).

title:
The Hearing Tree
A Structural Equilibrium Framework for Hearing Loss, Emotional Compression, Treatment Adoption, and Multi-Participant Healthcare Architecture
affiliations: Equinox Liquidity Suite

detail.title:
The Hearing Tree
A Structural Equilibrium Framework for Hearing Loss, Emotional Compression, Treatment Adoption, and Multi-Participant Healthcare Architecture

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could be perceived to have influenced the work presented in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study is a conceptual and theoretical framework and does not involve human participants, patient data, interventions, or identifiable case studies.

detail.abstract:
Hearing care is traditionally examined through clinical, psychological, or operational variables, yet the field exhibits system-wide patterns—delayed help-seeking, burnout waves, adoption fluctuations, and coordinated responses to economic cycles—that cannot be explained by isolated factors. This paper introduces The Hearing Tree Model, a structural-equilibrium framework derived from the Liquidity Tree architecture, which reconceptualizes hearing care as a multi-participant equilibrium system rather than a set of independent behaviors.

Each participant in the ecosystem is represented as a Liquidity Tree composed of roots (underlying biological, emotional, organisational, or economic pressures), an equilibrium stem (where tension accumulates or releases), and branches (observable behaviors and outcomes). These trees interact through a shared structural layer, the Master Equilibrium Axis (MEA), which distributes tension and synchronizes system response. Through this lens, phenomena such as resistance, burnout, workflow friction, leadership instability, supply disruptions, reimbursement friction, and macroeconomic contraction are not independent problems but structurally coupled expressions of the same equilibrium environment.

The Hearing Tree frames hearing-care systems as equilibrium-seeking organisms shaped by flows of emotional, operational, organisational, and economic energy. Compression in any part of the system propagates through the MEA and reshapes participant behavior, while expansion produces synchronized recovery. By providing a unified structural framework that integrates insights from clinical science, behavioural economics, organisational psychology, and macroeconomic modelling, the model establishes a foundation for system-level analysis and introduces hypotheses and measurement strategies capable of identifying structural strain before deterioration occurs.

The Hearing Tree positions hearing care not as a fragmented discipline but as a structurally interpretable ecosystem governed by universal equilibrium principles. This is a conceptual working paper; it advances testable hypotheses and a measurement scaffold without asserting empirical proof or clinical prescription.

title: AI-Driven Autonomous Network Architectures for Real-Time, Secure, and Fault-Tolerant Global Connectivity

detail.title: AI-Driven Autonomous Network Architectures for Real-Time, Secure, and Fault-Tolerant Global Connectivity
detail.abstract: The rapid growth of global communication systems demands network architectures capable of real-time decision-making, autonomous threat mitigation, and seamless fault tolerance. This study examines recent advances in AI-driven autonomous networking frameworks, including self-healing systems, real-time state synchronization protocols, federated zero-trust architectures, predictive fault-tolerant designs, and AI-enhanced intrusion detection systems. By synthesizing evidence from contemporary research, the paper demonstrates that combining AI-native orchestration, predictive analytics, and distributed intelligence significantly improves the reliability, security, and global coherence of next-generation networks. The findings highlight persistent gaps in interoperability, explainability, and multi-cloud integration while emphasizing the transformative potential of fully autonomous AI-driven architectures for global connectivity.

title: Federated AI Systems for Global Network Reliability: A Framework for Seamless Failover and Multi-Cloud Trust Enforcement

detail.title: Federated AI Systems for Global Network Reliability: A Framework for Seamless Failover and Multi-Cloud Trust Enforcement
detail.abstract: The growing reliance on multi-cloud architectures and globally distributed networks has introduced significant challenges in network reliability, latency, and trust enforcement. This study investigates federated artificial intelligence (AI) systems as a framework for ensuring seamless failover and enforcing multi-cloud trust. By integrating Real-Time State Information Exchange Protocol (RTSIX), Cognitive Autonomous Networking (CAN), AI-Native Zero-Trust Architecture (AI-ZTA), and adaptive AI-driven on-demand packet inspection, the study identifies a unified approach to improving network resilience. The findings indicate that federated AI systems significantly reduce failover time, optimize latency, and enforce cognitive trust across diverse cloud environments, highlighting their potential for critical infrastructure and financial systems. The study concludes that a federated AI framework provides a viable pathway for enhancing global network reliability and security, though further research is required for real-world large-scale deployment (Balakrishnan, 2022; Balakrishnan, 2024).

title: Designing Next-Generation Cognitive Internet Infrastructure: Redundancy, Security, and Adaptive Traffic Intelligence

detail.title: Designing Next-Generation Cognitive Internet Infrastructure: Redundancy, Security, and Adaptive Traffic Intelligence
detail.abstract: The rapid escalation in global connectivity demands an Internet infrastructure capable of autonomous decision-making, predictive security enforcement, and seamless redundancy across multi-cloud ecosystems. This study develops a conceptual framework for next-generation cognitive Internet infrastructure by synthesizing research on self-learning network architectures, AI-native security models, real-time synchronization protocols, and adaptive traffic intelligence. The methodology integrates comparative architectural analysis of cognitive systems, zero-trust frameworks, and redundancy mechanisms documented in existing scholarly literature. Findings reveal that a unified cognitive architecture-supported by federated zero-trust enforcement, cross-vendor redundancy using real-time state synchronization, and adaptive AI-driven packet inspection-can significantly enhance Internet resilience, security posture, and traffic efficiency. The study concludes that transitioning to such infrastructures requires vendor-neutral interoperability standards, national-level digital policy reforms, and expanded research into autonomous routing optimization.

title: The $180 Billion ESOP Mistake: Why Target-Date Funds Fail America's Manufacturing Workers

detail.title: The $180 Billion ESOP Mistake: Why Target-Date Funds Fail America's Manufacturing Workers
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a fixed-weight lifecycle investment strategy-33% domestic equities and 67% international equities, drawn from robustness checks in Anarkulova, Cederburg, and O'Doherty (2025)-as a superior alternative to age-based target-date funds (TDFs) for manufacturing 401(k)s and Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs). This contra approach ignores "maturity" glide paths, which amplify IID pitfalls in conventional stock-bond allocations (Anarkulova et al., 2025, Table I). Using a nonparametric block bootstrap on 2,600+ years of global returns augmented with Compustat firm-level data for vertically integrated manufacturers (SIC 20-39, 1970-2024), the analysis simulates vertical firm cash flows with supply chain betas (Eun and Resnick, 1988). The fixed global equity portfolio outperforms balanced 60/40 benchmarks by 41% in terminal wealth and reduces ruin risk by 9.3% under a 4% withdrawal rule. ESOP extensions, calibrated to lifecycle models with employee ownership frictions (Dahlquist, Setty, and Vestman, 2018; Gomes, Michaelides, and Zhang, 2022), yield a 10.07% savings rate boost for participants to match optimal utility-equivalent to $2,800 annual gains per median worker. In an era of reshoring, vertical integration heightens domestic asset-labor correlations (Baxter and Jermann, 1997), making international equities the essential hedge over bonds (Brandes Institute, n.d.; Rempel, 2025). Policy: Replace TDF defaults in manufacturing plans with fixed global equity to unlock $180B in aggregate value (BDO, 2025; Job Quality Center, 2024).

title: Artificial Intelligence Revolution in Supply Chain Management: Navigating the Digital Transformation

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence Revolution in Supply Chain Management: Navigating the Digital Transformation
detail.abstract:
The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping supply chain management, transforming traditional linear and reactive systems into intelligent, adaptive, and predictive networks. In an era of increasing globalization, rising customer expectations, and operational complexity, organizations face unprecedented challenges in maintaining efficiency, resilience, and agility across their supply chains. This study explores the revolutionary role of AI in supply chain management and examines how digital transformation is redefining operational and strategic decision-making.

The paper analyzes AI as a cognitive layer that enhances supply chain ecosystems by continuously processing vast amounts of structured and unstructured data to generate real-time insights. Technologies such as machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning enable predictive intelligence, allowing organizations to shift from reactive problem-solving to anticipatory operations. AI-driven demand forecasting, predictive maintenance, and autonomous decision-making systems significantly improve accuracy, speed, and responsiveness, enabling businesses to optimize inventory, production planning, and logistics performance.

In addition to operational benefits, the research highlights the strategic advantages of AI integration, including improved forecasting precision, enhanced customer service, increased financial performance, and sustainable competitive differentiation. AI-powered supply chains demonstrate superior adaptability, allowing organizations to respond effectively to market changes, product lifecycle variations, and geographic expansion. These capabilities contribute to revenue growth, cost reduction, better asset utilization, and stronger organizational resilience.

However, the study also emphasizes the substantial challenges associated with AI implementation. High financial investment requirements, organizational resistance, cultural barriers, technical integration complexity, data governance issues, cybersecurity risks, and regulatory compliance concerns present significant obstacles. The paper discusses algorithmic limitations, data dependency, and the risks of over-reliance on automated systems, particularly in times of unprecedented disruption. Furthermore, the difficulty in accurately measuring AI-driven value and the long payback periods required for successful implementation are critically examined.

The study concludes that while AI offers transformative potential for supply chain management, successful adoption requires a balanced, strategic, and human-centered approach. Organizations must invest not only in technology, but also in data quality, workforce development, governance structures, and change management. By aligning AI initiatives with clear business objectives and ethical considerations, organizations can achieve sustainable competitive advantage and long-term value creation in the digital economy.

title: Government Waste Exceeds Military Budget: NEW Contra Reform 92% Accurate Framework Saves $2.2 Trillion + 146M Tons of CO2 (All of Belgium's Annual Emissions) in Manufacturing

detail.abstract: Government waste in manufacturing now exceeds the military budget ($850B), with $2.2 trillion in CHIPS Act and infrastructure spending enabling crony capitalism rather than productive capacity. This toxic culture of political favoritism-where connected entities capture subsidies regardless of merit-is making the American manufacturing economy sick. I demonstrate that crony capitalism creates $47 billion annual waste while preventing 146 million tons of CO2 savings-equivalent to Belgium's entire annual emissions-through production inefficiencies. This is not politics-this is corruption masquerading as industrial policy. A healthy economy rewards efficiency and innovation; our current system rewards lobbying expenditures ($450M return per $1M spent) and political connections. The framework reveals systematic misallocation in CHIPS Act implementation, where politically connected entities capture 73% of major awards despite representing only 12% of eligible manufacturers. Analysis shows manufacturing capacity utilization remains 3.6 percentage points below historical averages (75.9% vs. 79.5% long-run) despite massive federal investment. Industrial production declined 1.5% net from February 2020 through August 2025. Key Innovation: I developed the Artificial Vertical Market Integration (AVMI) framework achieving 92% accuracy in predicting major enforcement actions in healthcare, then extended it to manufacturing. During Quantitative Tightening (QT), I documented a 23 percentage point credit access premium for politically connected firms (p<0.001)-not because they're more efficient (they have 10pp LOWER productivity), but because they invested in political relationships rather than manufacturing capability. The fixed-weight equity allocation strategy (33% domestic/67% international) I developed for manufacturing pension participants positions workers to benefit from legitimate productivity gains while avoiding rent extraction. Implementation would save $380-520 billion over 10 years while enabling 2.8-3.4 million jobs through merit-based investment. The choice is stark: Healthy economy through merit-based competition, or hospice economy extracting rent while manufacturing dies. The framework demonstrates how economic efficiency and climate leadership align through optimized domestic production, eliminating false trade-offs between competitiveness and environmental goals.

title: Media as Translator: Deconstructing Ophelia in the Era of Taylor Swift
affiliations: Guruvayurappan College

detail.title: Media as Translator: Deconstructing Ophelia in the Era of Taylor Swift

detail.abstract: This paper examines the significant role of media as a translator of meaning, focusing on how classical literary texts and figures are reinterpreted within the digital culture, enabling the translation of experience into new forms. It meditates on how the media participation, like interactive media and music video, critically interpreted and received the work. And how the representation of female agency and identity has changed today. Using Shakespeare's Ophelia from the 17th century and the popular pop persona of Taylor Swift from the 21st century as a comparative framework. This research examines how Modern Digital media, through music videos, social platforms, and interactive media, reshape and subvert traditional narratives, such as patriarchy, into contemporary discourses of female agency and identity. By analyzing the tragic Portrayal of Ophelia in Hamlet and contrasting it with Taylor Swift's self-represented narrative of recovery, empowerment, resistance, and self-authorship, the research paper enlightens how the subjectivity of female experience transforms under media. This is woven to the notion of Marshall McLuhan's ₋ media as an extension of human perception, permitting translation of experience into new forms. This interdisciplinary inquiry reveals how traditional conservative literary texts are renegotiated and reconstructed into a cultural framework. This flips the gender dynamics and presents a reclamation of voice through participatory media. This analysis proclaims the urgency and necessity of understanding media not as a static document but as a performative and informative agent with political stakes in narrative representation

detail.title: Analyzing the Impact of Online Reviews on Consumer Purchase Decisions
detail.abstract: Online reviews are user-generated feedback shared on digital platforms that help consumers evaluate a product or service before making a purchase decision. This research investigates the impact of online reviews on the purchase decisions of the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Valenzuela (PLV) students. The study employs the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) to analyze the correlations among the variables: online reviews, attitude towards behavior, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and purchase intention in assessing product or service purchases. A quantitative research method was utilized, incorporating surveys with 212 participants selected from third-year students of the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Valenzuela (PLV) in Valenzuela City, Metro Manila, Philippines. The research reveals that consumers generally perceive online reviews positively in their purchase decisions (overall mean: 3.47), although their behavioral response was lower (overall mean: 3.38), especially regarding attitudes (mean: 3.44). Perception was strongest for credibility and reliability (mean: 3.56), followed by quantity and consistency (mean: 3.49), and expertise and authenticity (mean: 3.42). Statistical analysis indicated that the perception of credibility and reliability (r = 0.365, p = 0.000) and quantity and consistency (r = 0.540, p = 0.000) significantly impacted consumer attitude. Furthermore, expertise and authenticity showed a lesser, but still significant, link (r = 0.474, p = 0.000). In addition, qualitative analysis identified significant barriers, such as fake reviews, lack of reviewer credibility, limited details or vague feedback, and information overload, which lead to customer reluctance in embracing online purchasing behaviors. The research highlights the necessity for improved consumer education and targeted marketing for students and consumers to avoid any inconvenience when purchasing online. Recommendations encompass localized involvement techniques, relationship-building with sellers, and improved product information to enhance consumer awareness. By overcoming these obstacles, online shopping websites may enhance consumers' positive perceptions of online purchasing behaviors.

title: Forecasting Consumer Demand for Electronics on Amazon Using Google Trends and Web Traffic Data
affiliations: , Sichuan University and University of the People

detail.title: Forecasting Consumer Demand for Electronics on Amazon Using Google Trends and Web Traffic Data
detail.abstract: Demand forecasting for consumer electronics remains a critical challenge in e-commerce due to rapid innovation cycles and volatile consumer preferences. Traditional time-series models rely exclusively on historical transaction data, overlooking the behavioral signals that precede actual purchases. This study proposes an integrated forecasting framework that combines Google Trends search interest and SimilarWeb traffic engagement metrics with classical and machine learning approaches to enhance prediction accuracy for electronics demand on Amazon. Using weekly data spanning three years across North America, Europe, and East Asia, we develop and compare traditional statistical models (ARIMA), machine learning algorithms (XGBoost, Random Forest), deep learning networks (LSTM), and hybrid architectures (ARIMA-XGBoost). Granger causality analysis reveals that search intensity exhibits a 2-week lead time in predicting sales fluctuations, while web traffic engagement demonstrates concurrent predictive power. The hybrid ARIMA-XGBoost model incorporating behavioral features achieves a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) reduction of 14.3% compared to baseline ARIMA, with consistent performance across geographic markets. These findings demonstrate that publicly accessible behavioral data functions as a form of market transparency that improves forecasting accuracy without requiring proprietary datasets. The research contributes to both academic literature on information economics and practical decision-making for e-commerce businesses, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises seeking cost-effective demand intelligence tools.

detail.abstract:
Background: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) and intrathecal baclofen pump (ITB) implants are neurosurgical-neuromodulation therapies for refractory dystonia with limited data available on the decision-making process for children and young people (CYP). We examine the clinical characteristics, reasons for not proceeding with the DBS/ITB programme, the time taken for decision-making, and other influential factors.

Methods: Retrospective review of routinely collected clinical data of 759 CYP screened between 2007 and 2023, classified according to aetiology of dystonia and chosen therapeutic route. Reasons for and against DBS/ITB were reviewed. Factors contributing to the probability of undergoing DBS/ITB were analysed using logistic regression. The influence of baseline Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) level, dystonia aetiology, age of patients, and years of unit experience on time-to-decision were analysed using Cox regression.

Findings: Of 759 referred CYP, 42% underwent DBS/ITB (79% DBS, 21% ITB), 51% did not proceed, and 7% remained under evaluation. Genetic dystonia was the most common aetiology in the DBS group (39%), whereas acquired dystonia predominated in both the non-neurosurgical (67%) and ITB groups (78%). DBS/ITB was deemed unsuitable due to medical background (65%), patient/family decision (23·5%), abnormal ancillary investigations (10%) and insufficient expected gain (3.5%). Genetic aetiology significantly increased the likelihood of DBS/ITB (Odds Ratio= 3·64, p < 0·001), while older remission age was associated with shorter time-to-decision (Hazard Ratio = 1·06, p < 0·001).

Interpretation: There was a high exclusion rate for DBS for acquired dystonia, consistent with the greater variability and less certainty of positive outcomes compared to genetic dystonia to guide decision-making. Patient/family rejection was the second most common reason for exclusion from DBS/ITB. Decision-making time shortened with increasing age at referral, this should inform service planning for timely, individualised care for CYP with dystonia.

detail.abstract: The rapid growth of Buy-Now-Pay-Later (BNPL) options affects how people respond, particularly digitally active students. This research focuses on understanding BNPL options and their effects on gadget purchase frequency and promotional redemption among college students. It is grounded in Prospect Theory and examines how individuals' perceptions of changes brought about by payment convenience and perceived risk influence their buying decisions. The research employed a quantitative correlational approach to gather data from a total of 388 respondents through a structured survey questionnaire. The findings reveal that students have generally positive attitudes toward BNPL. Respondents strongly agreed with statements regarding ease of use (overall mean = 3.27) and perceived financial risk and gain (mean = 3.27), while payment convenience obtained a slightly lower mean (3.23). The data also indicate that BNPL leads to favorable consumer behavior, as gadget purchase frequency (mean = 2.76) and promotional redemption (mean = 3.05) increased. Statistical analysis revealed significant correlations between BNPL perceptions and purchasing outcomes. Payment convenience showed a moderate-to-strong relationship with promotional redemption (r = 0.555, p < 0.001), while accessibility had a substantial effect on both purchase frequency and promotional redemption. Although students recognized risks such as overspending, they continued using BNPL because they perceived it as manageable and financially flexible. This research highlights the need to improve financial literacy, establish guidelines for responsible BNPL use, and implement marketing interventions aligned with student behavior. The proposed recommendations include improved BNPL disclosures, spending alerts, platform-based educational campaigns, and student-focused promotional activities. Addressing these concerns can help retailers and fintech providers support informed decision-making while promoting students' financial well-being in an expanding digital marketplace.

title: Strategic Resilience During Trade Policy Volatility: A Capability-Based Framework for Competitive Advantage
affiliations: and O. P. Jindal Global University

detail.title: Strategic Resilience During Trade Policy Volatility: A Capability-Based Framework for Competitive Advantage
detail.abstract:
Purpose: A Trade Policy Resilience (TPR) framework is introduced in this paper as a strategic response to rising trade policy volatility. It redefines resilience from risk mitigation to a dynamic capability that helps firms maintain commitments, grow market share, and lead ecosystems during disruptions.
Design/Methodology/Approach: The framework was developed through practice-based theory building, drawing on long-term consulting engagements with Global 1000 enterprises. It includes ten dimensions and thirty capabilities that together define an enterprise's resilience maturity. Validation is demonstrated through a comparative case analysis of four multinational firms (Intel, Toyota, Peloton, and BASF), showing differences in TPR maturity and strategic outcomes. Validation of the framework across industries, continents, and scales was conducted using five companies as case examples (BYD Automotive, Tonies, Apple, O'Reilly, and Cisco). A structured diagnostic tool supports organisational self-assessment and capability development.
Findings: Firms with high TPR maturity incorporate resilience into strategic planning, enabling proactive responses to trade policy shocks. The framework links supply chain diversification, regulatory agility, financial hedging, and stakeholder trust to achieving a competitive advantage. Case evidence indicates that resilience is not merely about operational continuity but also serves as a form of strategic differentiation.
Practical Implications: CEOs and COOs, as well as risk leaders, can apply the TPR framework to integrate resilience into their competitive strategy formulation. It promotes cross-functional alignment and investment priorities in volatile global markets.
Originality/Value: This study contributes to the literature on dynamic capabilities and strategic resilience by providing a scalable and diagnostic framework for adapting trade policy. It bridges theory and practice, providing a tool for both scholarly inquiry and executive decision-making.

title: The Strategic Convergence: Risk-Adaptive AI for Reducing Insider Exfiltration and Improving Forensic Readiness

detail.title: The Strategic Convergence: Risk-Adaptive AI for Reducing Insider Exfiltration and Improving Forensic Readiness

detail.abstract:
The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into enterprise and defense environments has fundamentally expanded the insider threat attack surface. Traditional “collect everything” surveillance architectures generate alert fatigue, increase legal and privacy risk, and consistently fail to preempt low-signal, high-impact insider activity. This paper argues for a strategic pivot from universal visibility toward Precision Engagement: a risk-adaptive architecture that combines records governance, targeted monitoring, and mathematically assured AI.

The paper introduces an integrated operational doctrine built on four pillars: (1) a 30-day forensic “Safe Harbor” for deleted data aligned with DoD records management standards; (2) strict bifurcation of administrative and investigative records to reduce liability and preserve evidentiary integrity; (3) trigger-based User Activity Monitoring consistent with civil-liberties constraints; and (4) predictive “Mission Graphs” that model risk as anomalous access paths rather than isolated events. To ensure defensibility, the framework mandates Expected Calibration Error (ECE) thresholds for AI risk scoring and embeds circuit-breaker patterns to prevent automated harm.

The result is a deployable governance and technical model that improves detection latency, reduces false positives, and preserves trust while remaining compatible with existing DoD, Intelligence Community, and Defense Industrial Base authorities.

detail.abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of performance management practices in Bangladesh, focusing on the public sector (PWD Bangladesh) and the private sector (RFL Bangladesh). Performance management is critical for aligning individual contributions with organizational objectives, enhancing employee productivity, and fostering continuous improvement. The research highlights core components such as goal setting, performance monitoring, feedback, appraisals, learning and development, recognition, and performance improvement plans. Through qualitative interviews with key personnel from both organizations, the study identifies sector-specific practices, challenges, and strategies. Findings reveal that while the private sector adopts structured, data-driven, and outcomeoriented performance management systems emphasizing employee development and digital integration, the public sector faces challenges including bureaucratic constraints, limited financial incentives, and political interference. Despite these challenges, initiatives such as online tracking, feedback loops, and non-monetary recognition demonstrate efforts toward improving efficiency and accountability. The study underscores the importance of adopting context-appropriate strategies, fostering a culture of continuous improvement, and leveraging lessons from both sectors to enhance organizational effectiveness in Bangladesh. The research contributes to understanding how performance management practices can be tailored to sectoral and cultural contexts in developing countries.

detail.abstract:
Background: Traditional approaches to personal transformation often fail to produce sustainable outcomes due to limited integration of biological, cognitive, and systems-based mechanisms. The disconnection between cognitive interventions and underlying neurophysiological substrates contributes to high relapse rates and short-lived behavioural change. 

Objective: This paper introduces the Sustainable Self-Redesign (SSR) Model™, an interdisciplinary framework integrating autonomic regulation, cognitive restructuring, neural pattern interruption, and systems-level alignment to support durable identity transformation. 

Methods: The SSR Model™ was developed through a three-phase, iterative process: (1) theoretical integration of established scientific frameworks across stress physiology, REBT, NLP, and systems thinking; (2) applied self-experimentation and informal implementation; and (3) a structured pilot study with high-achieving professionals (N=20) conducted in Düsseldorf, Germany (2024-2025). 

Results: Preliminary findings indicate meaningful improvements across multiple domains, including reduced perceived stress, decreased endorsement of irrational beliefs, increased authentic self-alignment, and improved autonomic nervous system regulation (supported by HRV data when available). Qualitative analysis further demonstrated shifts in identity coherence, relational patterns, and long-term behavioural alignment at 12-week follow-up. 

Conclusions: The SSR Model™ represents a novel integration of biological, cognitive, and systems sciences applied to personal transformation. By targeting identity architecture-rather than isolated behaviours-the model offers a scientifically grounded pathway for sustainable change. While early results are promising, further research employing controlled designs, larger samples, and extended follow-up is warranted.

title: Resource Allocation Optimization for Disaster Medical Systems Based on Open BCMP Queueing Networks
affiliations: Juntendo University and Chuo University

detail.title: Resource Allocation Optimization for Disaster Medical Systems Based on Open BCMP Queueing Networks
detail.abstract: During large-scale disasters, the simultaneous influx of patients overwhelms medical systems, causing prolonged waiting times and deteriorated outcomes. This study develops an evaluation framework for disaster medical response by integrating an open BCMP queueing network, a gravity model, and two-stage optimization.The open BCMP network captures patient flow from affected areas through first-aid stations and ambulance transport to hospitals. The gravity model reflects facility selection based on distance and capacity. The framework incorporates four patient severity classes with triage-based transitions and heterogeneous service disciplines (FCFS, PS, IS). A two-stage lexicographic optimization first guarantees system stability, then minimizes congestion variation under budget constraints using simulated annealing.Numerical experiments on a virtual region (1,040 zones, 35 facilities) demonstrate substantial improvement in objective function values and system stability across casualty rates of 0.5--3.5%. Ambulance vehicles consistently account for 75--90% of required resource increases, identifying transport capacity as the structural bottleneck. Application to real-world data from a Japanese regional medical area demonstrates that the framework successfully adapts to actual population distributions, facility locations, and road networks, yielding optimization results that appropriately reflect regional characteristics.The framework provides quantitative decision support for disaster medical planning, including resource stockpile allocation and ambulance deployment strategies, demonstrating the applicability of BCMP network analysis to complex medical systems under resource constraints.

title: Deployable Unsupervised Deep-Learning System for Real-Time Health Monitoring of Semiconductor Air Compressors
affiliations: National Tsing Hua University, National Tsing Hua University,  and

detail.title: Deployable Unsupervised Deep-Learning System for Real-Time Health Monitoring of Semiconductor Air Compressors
detail.abstract: Semiconductor fabs rely on air compressors as critical utilities whose unexpected failures can disrupt production and induce costly tool downtime. Yet air-compressor condition data are typically highdimensional, non-stationary, and largely unlabeled, making supervised fault classification difficult in practice. This paper presents a deployable prognostics and health management (PHM) framework for real-time predictive maintenance of semiconductor air compressors using unsupervised deep learning. The approach integrates (i) temperature deseasonalization to reduce environmental confounding, (ii) a deep autoencoder trained on historical healthy behavior, and (iii) an expert-informed, weighted reconstructionerror health indicator that is mapped to an interpretable 0–100 health score. A two-level warning logic, combining a moving-average health drop criterion with absolute health thresholds, supports both early cautionary alerts and urgent intervention flags. A real-world case study using multi-year sensor data from seven compressors in a semiconductor plant demonstrates how the proposed health score and visualization dashboard enable continuous monitoring, anomaly localization by contributing parameters, and maintenance decision support (e.g., identifying periods where major maintenance could plausibly be deferred when health remains stable). The proposed framework is practical for industrial settings where labeled faults are scarce, interpretability is required, and real-time operation is essential.

title: A Comprehensive Review of Reinforcement Learning Methodologies and their impact on modern healthcare practices
affiliations: , Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Roorkee and Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Roorkee

detail.title: A Comprehensive Review of Reinforcement Learning Methodologies and their impact on modern healthcare practices
detail.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) takes inspiration from how humans and animals learn through rewards and consequences, much like psychological studies of behavior. Picture a smart system that starts out knowing very little about its surroundings, but through trial and error, it gradually figures out the best way to make decisions - that's  essentially what modern reinforcement learning does using mathematical models. What's really exciting is how this approach is now transforming real-world fields like healthcare, where it's helping doctors create personalized treatment plans, improve diagnostic accuracy, and manage hospital resources more efficiently. The progress we've seen in recent years has been truly remarkable. In general, RL offers a solid platform for improving the efficiency and precision of medical solutions opening new avenues for solving challenging problems in a wide range of fields. The paper gives an in-depth overview of reinforcement learning methods, studying their distinct characteristics and strengths over conventional dynamic programming. We review their efficacy in solving real-world challenges, particularly, in the field of medicine. RL has improved this domain enormously through the ability to understand and react to real-world information where it can facilitate adaptive treatment strategies, accurate medical diagnoses, and optimized utilization of resources.

title: Systematic Literature Review of Particle Therapy Costing: Two Decades of Evidence on Costing Methods and Analytical Assumptions
affiliations: Ghent University, Ghent University - Department of Accountancy and Corporate Finance, Ghent University, Ghent University, Ghent University, KU Leuven, UZ Leuven and Ghent University Hospital - Department of Radiation Oncology

detail.title: Systematic Literature Review of Particle Therapy Costing: Two Decades of Evidence on Costing Methods and Analytical Assumptions
detail.abstract: Particle therapy is an advanced type of external beam radiotherapy, using charged particles such as protons or heavy ions, expectedly offering significant clinical advantages in cancer treatment. Adopting innovative technologies, such as particle therapy, in clinical practice, requires economic evidence. Data on the actual cost of standard or innovative radiotherapy interventions are however scarce, and no consistent guidelines exist on costing approaches in this field. This systematic review evaluates the methodologies and analytical assumptions used in costing studies of particle therapy, to inform a standardized costing framework.  A comprehensive search was conducted across four databases to identify studies that included original cost data, applying strict inclusion criteria to ensure relevance. Data extraction focused on costing methods and analytical assumptions of the selected studies, with no focus on reported costing figures.  The selection process resulted in the inclusion of 12 studies. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in underlying assumptions of the analysis and costing methods. Despite this variability, the studies had high scores in quality assessments. The review findings highlight the need for recommendations to standardize costing in particle therapy. Such standardization is essential to facilitate robust economic evaluations and support evidence-based reimbursement decisions.

title: Structural Tension Theory: A Meta-Diagnostic Framework for Matching Psychological Intervention to Tension Architecture
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Structural Tension Theory: A Meta-Diagnostic Framework for Matching Psychological Intervention to Tension Architecture

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. The author is employed in an unrelated industry (information security) and has no financial interests in psychotherapy training, certification, or clinical practice.
